bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Deterministic source-free local reasoning over the exact predecessor reasoning STATE plus the already-authorized role-local repository CAS/readback transport. semantic_fields.parent_blob: Exact blob SHA of the role-local STATE from which this candidate was derived.

minimal_checkpoint_schema.transport_precondition: Read current role-local STATE as H; accept candidate C only if C.parent_blob=blob(H), C.slice_id!=H.slice_id, and C.o3 satisfies the invariant; commit using CAS sha=blob(H); exact-read back the resulting STATE once.
minimal_checkpoint_schema.minimality_claim: For the local stale/duplicate-predecessor problem, parent_blob is the single freshness discriminator, slice_id distinguishes successor identity, and the two O3 bits are the minimal three-class diagnostic established by the predecessor slice. No extra counter, lock, lease, queue, hosted coordinator, or external primitive is required.

bounded_leaf_result.stale_predecessor_rejection: If any newer STATE H1 has replaced H0, a candidate derived from H0 carries parent_blob=blob(H0). The acceptance predicate against H1 fails before write, and repository CAS with sha=blob(H0) also fails. Thus stale predecessors cannot overwrite a newer role-local checkpoint.
bounded_leaf_result.duplicate_replay_rejection: After candidate C is committed, the current STATE is C with a new blob. Replaying the same C still names its old parent, so parent_blob!=blob(current) and the old CAS sha is invalid. A duplicate successor is therefore rejected rather than committed twice.
bounded_leaf_result.crash_replay_property: A crash before commit leaves H unchanged, so the same candidate may be reconstructed on the next invocation from fresh bootstrap and retried once. A crash after commit but before local acknowledgment leaves C as current STATE; fresh read observes C, so replay of the old-parent candidate is rejected. Exact readback distinguishes the successful-commit path when the connector returns normally.
bounded_leaf_result.o3_preservation: The checkpoint stores only the already-derived observational code. R maps to [0,0], P to [1,0], W to [1,1]; [0,1] is rejected as inconsistent with the stage-labeled transition relation.

cr14b_noninterference.field_disjointness: parent_blob, slice_id, reached_CR14a and cr14a_mismatch are role-local checkpoint metadata and do not write S.tail.ordinal, last_consumed_ordinal, summary_identity, boundary-link inputs, or any other CR14b predicate field.
cr14b_noninterference.P: P records O3=[1,0] and reaches q14b_ready with all CR14b-relevant fields unchanged from the predecessor model.
cr14b_noninterference.W: W records O3=[1,1] only after the modeled CR14a mismatch terminates the trace; CR14b remains unreachable but its formula and inputs are untouched.
cr14b_noninterference.R: R records O3=[0,0] on the pre-CR14a termination path; CR14b remains unreachable and unchanged.
cr14b_noninterference.conclusion: Adding the checkpoint envelope changes persistence/diagnostic metadata only, so CR14b remains observationally noninterfering within the tested verifier model.

bounded_leaf_result.scope_limit: This establishes crash/replay safety only for the role-local checkpoint update itself. It does not make a separate externally visible side effect exactly-once. A crash after an external effect but before authoritative effect acknowledgment would still require the frozen generation-keyed idempotent effect primitive or equivalent current evidence; no such capability is claimed here.
